sections.content: How many people are "other vocational and industrial trainers"?

113,170 people

were counted on the census as "other vocational and industrial trainers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Other vocational and industrial trainers provide instruction in manual skills and other vocational skills, and advise on and organise vocational instruction within industrial, commercial and other establishments.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "other vocational and industrial trainers", 14% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other vocational and industrial trainers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other vocational and industrial trainers" included:

  • cleaning and housekeeping managers and supervisors
  • welfare professionals (other)
  • health associate professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "other vocational and industrial trainers" there were a similar number of men and women (48.2% compared with 51.8%).

This means "other vocational and industrial trainers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 48.2% and women made up 51.8% of "other vocational and industrial trainers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other vocational and industrial trainers" included:

  • textiles, garments and related trades (other)
  • dental practitioners
  • travel agency managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "other vocational and industrial trainers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "other vocational and industrial trainers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other vocational and industrial trainers", 11.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (76.2% compared with 23.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (84.5%) than self-employed (15.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
